correctness.rationale: O(d) symmetry gives the orthogonal direct sum span{1,t}, span{x_i}, and harmonic quadratics, and the exact radial generalized eigenproblem Bv=lambda Mv. The nonradial eigenvalues are lambda1=b1/mu and lambda2=b2/nu. The diagonal B-lambda1 M=diag(b0-lambda1,b2-nu lambda1) proves the two necessary-and-sufficient weak moment inequalities and all strict/equality cases, including lambda_rad,+>=lambda2. Sliding-interval conditional means with positive density are strictly increasing, yielding exactly two thin-shell crossings for small width at each fixed dimension and the displayed epsilon^2 shifts. For d=2, exact radical integration over [0,u] union [1/2,v] gives moments (1/2,1/4,1/6) and scalar energy one-half for every degree<=2 polynomial. Independent exact computations confirmed diagonal algebra, 12 rational-mask cases and radical moments; the proof, not finite samples, establishes all-mask claims.

value.rationale: The leading eigenspace of a natural polynomial concentration operator undergoes two exact angular transitions under thin-shell location, and the half-transmission disk/annulus supplies an exact nontrivial spectral-indistinguishability example. final_claim: For every radial [0,1]-valued mask on the real unit ball and polynomial degree at most two, the concentration spectrum decomposes exactly into radial, linear and harmonic-quadratic sectors; the linear sector dominates iff b1/b0>=mu and b2/b1<=nu/mu, with exact equality multiplicities, two thin-shell transitions and a nonconstant disk mask with scalar concentration one half.
